cf.title: pg_upgrade doesn't copy ICU rules on template0

input.subject: pg_upgrade doesn't copy ICU rules on template0

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a or 1b: the bug is stated, a user reported it, and the fix completes what pg_upgrade already does for template0's other locale fields. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-1, is a fixable level 2 point about patch shape: v1 puts the daticurules fix and a rewrite of shared query and logging helpers in one commit that is requested for backpatch to 16. A committer has to decide what goes to stable branches.

brief.title: pg_upgrade: copy daticurules of template0 to the new cluster
brief.problem: Since 16, pg_upgrade copies the old template0's encoding and locale fields into the new template0, but it skips daticurules. A cluster initialized with --icu-rules loses those rules on template0 after an upgrade. This affects users who set ICU rules at initdb time.
brief.proposed_design: set_locale_and_encoding() adds daticurules to its existing UPDATE of template0, with the value escaped by PQescapeLiteral(). The query and logging buffers in pg_upgrade switch to StringInfo so they grow for long rules. The patch also removes the branches on target cluster version, since pg_upgrade only supports its own major version as target.
user_visible_surface: pg_upgrade now carries template0's daticurules into the new cluster.
pg_upgrade error and log messages no longer truncate long queries or long rules.
Separate patch in message #7: CREATE DATABASE with a non-ICU provider no longer inherits ICU rules from the template.
author_claims: The omission was an oversight in commit 30a53b792959, which added ICU rules.
Using executeQueryOrDie() keeps the full query with inlined values in error reports.
The target-version branches in set_locale_and_encoding() are unnecessary.
A reporter tested v1 on master and found pg_upgrade works.
The fix needs a backport to 16; the CREATE DATABASE fix needs a backport to 17.
brief.thread_state: Tom Lane first questioned how template0 can change, and Shihao explained that pg_upgrade itself updates it. Heikki agreed the fix is right but asked why template0 keeps locale fields at all, and found a CREATE DATABASE bug that Shihao addressed in a second patch.
unclear: The material does not show tests for multiline or long ICU rules.
The material does not say whether the StringInfo buffer change and errno handling go into back branches.
The material does not say whether the CREATE DATABASE fix belongs in this CommitFest entry or a separate one.
No one has said whether the design question about locale fields on template0 blocks this fix.

objections.title: Back-branch fix bundles unrelated pg_upgrade refactoring
objections.failure_scenario: A committer backpatches v1 to 16 as one unit. It brings the StringInfo rewrite of the query and logging buffers in util.c and server.c, the errno change and the removal of the target-version branches. A regression in pg_log() or executeQueryOrDie() then reaches every pg_upgrade run on stable branches, not only clusters that use ICU rules.
objections.argument: The bug needs one more column in an existing UPDATE, but v1 also changes the shared logging and query helpers that every pg_upgrade step uses. The commit message lists all of it as one change, and message #5 asks for a backport to 16 without saying which parts go back. Heikki in message #1 suggested growing the buffers as a possible fix, but he expected ICU rules to stay short. Keeping the general refactoring on master only would limit what stable branches take on.
objections.author_must_show: Can the series be split into a minimal daticurules fix for 16 and later, plus the buffer and branch cleanup for master only, or does the fix depend on the buffer change?

critic.reasoning: The v1 commit message puts the daticurules fix, the StringInfo buffer change, the errno change and the branch removal in one commit, and message #5 asks for a backport to 16. The thread does not say which parts go to stable branches.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: The patch changes what pg_upgrade writes into the new cluster's template0 row; no on-disk format changes.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: pg_upgrade now updates the existing pg_database.daticurules column for template0; no catalog schema change.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The fix is requested for 16 and later, and v1 bundles a StringInfo rewrite of shared helpers in util.c and server.c.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: v1 changes the query and logging helpers that every pg_upgrade step uses, and removes the target-version branches.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Can the series be split into a minimal daticurules fix for 16 and later, plus the buffer and branch cleanup for master only?
Does the daticurules fix depend on the StringInfo buffer change, and if so, at what rule length does the existing query buffer truncate?
Is there a test that upgrades a cluster initialized with multiline or long --icu-rules and checks template0's daticurules afterwards?
Should the CREATE DATABASE fix from message #7 go into this CommitFest entry or into a separate one with its own backpatch range?
Does the open question about why template0 keeps locale fields at all block this fix, or can the fix go in first?

committability.owner_note: Heikki Linnakangas started the thread, is the registered reviewer and agreed the fix is right; the owner needs to know pg_upgrade and the ICU locale fields in pg_database.
committability.liability: The owner signs for pg_upgrade behaviour on every stable branch from 16. If the StringInfo rewrite of the query and logging helpers is backpatched, that covers every pg_upgrade run, including clusters without ICU rules.
committability.author_follow_up: A v1 patch followed the review in message #1, and a second patch in message #7 addressed the CREATE DATABASE bug that Heikki found.

priority.reason: Only clusters initialized with --icu-rules are affected, but for them an upgrade silently drops template0's rules. The patch is about 10 KiB in five pg_upgrade files, a committer who knows the area is reviewing, and the open point is how to split it for backpatch.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review could not check that the source-version checks still handle old clusters before 16, or that the StringInfo change keeps the helpers' behaviour for other callers. The CREATE DATABASE patch in message #7 was not read.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade: Support for upgrading to checksums enabled
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets pg_upgrade run between clusters with different data checksum settings by rewriting page checksums while it copies files. The first version did this automatically in --copy mode, and a later version added an explicit --update-checksums option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author closed the entry because reviewers showed little interest in the feature or in solving its remaining problems. One problem was still open: copyFile() has a separate Windows code path, and the author did not know how checksum rewriting should work there. He said the feature could not move ahead without an answer to it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not sensing much enthusiasm for this feature or for working out the
remaining problems, so I'm closing this commitfest entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: add timing information to pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the elapsed time of each pg_upgrade step to the status output, for example "ok (took 82 ms)", formatted like psql's PrintTiming(). The goal was to show where upgrade time goes and to measure future work on reducing pg_upgrade downtime.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut questioned who besides developers would use the timings and said pg_upgrade output already has too much information that users cannot act on. He suggested that shell tools such as "pg_upgrade | ts" or "ts -i" are enough, and the author agreed to leave it at that unless someone saw a reason to build it in. Only a related fix that raised MESSAGE_WIDTH to 62 was committed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If it's just for developers and expert users, perhaps existing
shell-level functionality like "pg_upgrade | ts" would suffice?

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade documentation improvement
precedents_retrieved.summary: A documentation patch for pg_upgrade explained what "compatible initdb flags" means for the new cluster: the same encoding, locale and checksum settings as the old one. It told users to find the encoding and locale of template0 with psql -l and the checksum setting with pg_controldata.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut said the cluster locale is better taken from pg_controldata and doubted that pg_upgrade needs the encoding to match. The author asked whether to change the patch to use pg_controldata only, but no revised patch followed. Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback because the thread had died.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
A better way to get the
*cluster* locale is from pg_controldata.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade version and path checking
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set makes pg_upgrade check every executable it uses, require the new binaries to match pg_upgrade's exact major and minor version, and default --new-bindir to pg_upgrade's own directory. It came from Tom Lane's report that pg_upgrade 11.3 would use pg_dump 11.1.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut committed 0002 to 0004, which add the executable checks, the --new-bindir default and a typo fix. He found that 0001 compares pg_upgrade's version only with pg_ctl's, so it does not make all binaries match, and proposed a version check for each validate_exec() call instead. On 2019-09-02 the author said a new version would come that week, but no later version appears in the visible messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It compares (new_cluster.bin_version != PG_VERSION_NUM), but new_cluster.bin_version is actually just the version of pg_ctl, so this is just comparing the version of pg_upgrade with the version of pg_ctl, which is not wrong, but doesn't really achieve the full goal of having all binaries match.

precedents_retrieved.title: Backport perl tests for pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: Backport the Perl TAP version of the pg_upgrade tests (commit 322becb60) and related follow-up commits to REL_13_STABLE and REL_14_STABLE, replacing test.sh there. The goal was zero dump differences in cross-version upgrade tests, so users would not need to compare dumps by eye.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected that the TAP tests were new development that took several tries to get right on HEAD, so backporting them risks a test bug that hides a critical pg_upgrade issue. He preferred to keep further work on HEAD only, and the author withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If we were to backport
any of this, there is a risk of introducing a bug in what we do with
any of that, potentially hiding a issue critical related to
pg_upgrade.  That's not worth taking a risk for.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade allows itself to be run twice (initdb)
precedents_retrieved.summary: At the end of initdb, the patch sets NextOID in the control file to FirstNormalObjectId, so objects created in single-user mode cannot get OIDs that slip past pg_upgrade's check that the new cluster is empty. The author also proposed that pg_upgrade reject any changes made to the new cluster between initdb and pg_upgrade, which also stops a second pg_upgrade run on the same cluster.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut asked that the control file be updated directly with the controldata_utils.h functions instead of calling pg_resetwal. He also doubted that initdb needs to guard against use of postgres --single, which many consider deprecated outside initdb, and closed the entry as returned with feedback. No revised patch appears in the thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: However, I don't know whether we need to add special provisions that guard against people using postgres --single in complicated ways.  Many consider the single-user mode deprecated outside of initdb use.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade: Pass -j option down to vacuumdb
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Michael Paquier, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_upgrade pass its -j option to the vacuumdb commands in the generated analyze_new_cluster.sh script, so the post-upgrade analyze runs in parallel. Later versions added a VACUUM_OPTS variable to the script and a suggested vacuumdb --jobs command.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers held that pg_upgrade -j and vacuumdb -j are bound by different resources, so the same value should not be reused, and the generated script is meant to analyze gently. Tom Lane and Michael Paquier did not see most of the patch as better than the status quo and preferred a printed hint or a documentation-only change. The thread then moved to copying statistics in pg_upgrade instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: So based on that linking the value used by pg_upgrade and vacuumdb is a bad concept in my opinion, and the patch should be rejected.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix order of checking ICU options in initdb and create database
precedents_retrieved.summary: Reorder the validation of ICU-related options in initdb and CREATE DATABASE so that more fundamental errors (ICU not supported in this build, encoding not supported with ICU) are reported before a missing ICU locale. A later version narrowed this to an initdb encoding-check fix and added patches to document building without ICU as a marginal configuration and to build with ICU by default.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut objected that checking ICU support early adds more places where ICU support must be checked, increasing code size and future maintenance for what he considers a marginal configuration. He described the revised initdb.c changes as unprincipled code movement that breaks the existing structure, said the examples did not make clear what was being fixed, and rejected ICU-specific documentation and build-default changes in favor of a more general approach in a separate thread. The patch then waited on the author from December with no further revision and was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm concerned that the initdb.c changes are a bit unprincipled.  They
just move code around to achieve some behavior without keeping the
overall structure in mind.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P3] was a 2016 documentation patch about matching initdb flags, and its reason, getting the cluster locale from pg_controldata, does not apply to copying daticurules. Message #1 says the issue was split out of the pg_upgrade --initdb thread as an independent fix, and no earlier rejection of this fix is reported.

No user-facing contract changes beyond making pg_upgrade match what initdb already set. After upgrade, template0 again matches the old cluster, so `create database ... template template0` behaves as before. There is no new syntax, GUC, catalog column or psql change, and pg_dump never dumps template0, so the dump round-trip is unaffected. The separate CREATE DATABASE fix in message #7 only removes an error that blocks valid commands, so existing scripts do not change behaviour. A committer may want the StringInfo refactor kept out of the back-branch commit, but that is a question of patch shape, not of compatibility. This angle cannot check whether the source-version checks still handle sources older than 16.

Nothing in this proposal changes on-disk format, WAL, the replication protocol, the wire protocol, the catalog schema or any extension ABI. The fix writes an existing column, daticurules, into the new cluster's template0 during pg_upgrade, the same way 16 already writes the encoding and locale columns. The buffer change stays inside the frontend pg_upgrade binary. Source-version checks stay in place for clusters older than 16. One point could go in the release notes: clusters already upgraded under the bug have empty rules on template0, and this fix will not restore them.

No privilege or exposure aspect found. pg_upgrade runs as the cluster superuser, the rules come from the old cluster's template0, which only initdb sets, and PQescapeLiteral() quotes the value. Neither the larger buffers nor the CREATE DATABASE fix gives a non-superuser any new action or information.

The idea itself fits core. It fixes an omission in existing pg_upgrade code, adds nothing to hot paths, and a committer who knows the area (Heikki) is engaged as reviewer. The only concern from this angle is how the patch is split for backpatching.

Nothing in Postgres or a known extension already copies template0's daticurules during pg_upgrade. Running initdb with the same --icu-rules works around it today, but since 16 pg_upgrade copies template0's locale fields so that matching initdb options are not needed, and this patch completes that same mechanism instead of adding a second one. [P3] covers documentation for matching initdb flags and does not apply.

This is a bug fix for an existing feature, so the demand test does not apply. pg_upgrade already copies template0's encoding and locale fields, and only daticurules is skipped; a user report started the thread, and Heikki in messages #1 and #6 agrees it should be fixed. The affected group, clusters initialized with --icu-rules, is small, but the cost stays inside pg_upgrade, with no hot path, UI or catalog change.
